settings.label: Health Status
settings.help: Fallout 76 health and status presentation on the HUD.

settings.label: Fallout 4 Objective Popups
settings.help: Also show Fallout 4's objective list when objectives change. Fallout 76 shows those changes only in its quest tracker. Off needs Health Status, which draws that tracker.

settings.label: Weapon Condition
settings.help: Show the equipped weapon's condition bar on the HUD.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Crosshair
settings.help: Use Fallout 76's crosshair art, transitions and spread animation. Follows HUD Color and visibility settings.

settings.label: Floating Damage Numbers
settings.help: Show Fallout 76-style numbers at your hits using actual health damage. Critical, sneak and weak-point hits use the larger bonus animation. Works in power armor. Requires the converted status HUD.

settings.label: Show on Enemies
settings.help: Floating health, name, level, legendary stars and boss marker over visible enemies. Hides the top target bar while any floating healthbar group is enabled. Requires the updated converted status HUD.

settings.label: Show on Allies
settings.help: Floating healthbars for companions, teammates and settlers. Hides the top target bar while enabled.

settings.label: Show on Neutral
settings.help: Floating healthbars for other non-hostile actors. Hides the top target bar while enabled.

settings.label: Show Expanded Panel
settings.help: Show live current/maximum health and damage resistance icons in a centered box beneath the main target bar or floating healthbars. Works with all floating groups off. Zero resistances are hidden.

settings.label: Use Team Color
settings.help: Use a dedicated healthbar color for members of the Tales team system. Other allies and settlers keep their normal colors. Off follows the HUD color.

settings.label: Team Color
settings.help: Shared color for Tales team members' healthbars, names, badges and expanded details. Picking a color enables Use Team Color. Applies to floating bars and the main target bar.

settings.label: Legendary Item Announcements
settings.help: Fallout 76 banner when you pick up a legendary item.

settings.label: Quest Announcements
settings.help: Fallout 76 banners for quest and event completions, failures and rewards.

settings.label: Quest Start Announcements
settings.help: Fallout 76 "Quest Started" banner with the quest's Vault Boy when a quest or event begins.

settings.label: Location Discovery Announcements
settings.help: Fallout 76 "Discovered" banner when you find a new location.

settings.label: Favorites Wheel
settings.help: On: the Fallout 76 favorites wheel. Off: Fallout 4's stock favorites cross. Keeps your favorites and key binding.

settings.label: Dynamic Weapon Icons
settings.help: Favorites wheel and the HUD condition bar draw each weapon's own silhouette, attachments included, instead of a category icon. A weapon's first appearance shows the category icon while its silhouette is generated.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Pip-Boy Tabs
settings.help: Fallout 76 inventory tabs in the Pip-Boy.

settings.label: Items Listed on NEW
settings.help: How many recent pickups the NEW tab lists.

settings.label: Inspect Card
settings.help: Item card shown when inspecting. Equipment Condition always uses the Fallout 76 card.

settings.label: Inventory Enhancements
settings.help: Optional item icons, numeric columns, sorting and search in the converted inventory menus.

settings.label: Weight and Value Columns
settings.help: Compact WT, VAL and V/W columns. Click a heading to sort; click again to reverse.

settings.label: Item Icons
settings.help: Use generated item silhouettes with category icons while a model is loading.

settings.label: Colored Item Icons
settings.help: Color item icons by type. Off uses the menu color.

settings.label: Search
settings.help: Filter item names by all search words. Ctrl+F opens search; Escape clears it.

settings.label: Default Item Order
settings.help: Weight and value are per item. V/W uses value divided by unit weight.

settings.label: Largest First
settings.help: Start numeric sorting with the largest value first.

settings.label: Remember Item Order
settings.help: Keep each menu's chosen order until the game closes.

settings.label: Currency Trade
settings.help: Scrip, bullion, stamps and badge vendors.

settings.label: Quick Loot
settings.help: Apply the chosen item order to the entire loot list.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Main Menu
settings.help: Use BACUP-converted Fallout 76 menu art and music/video.

settings.label: Main Menu Music
settings.help: Random plays a different Fallout 76 theme on each main-menu visit. A track your conversion lacks plays a random one.

settings.label: Photo Loading Screens
settings.help: Show your ProSnap or Photo Mode photos during loading.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Loading Screens
settings.help: Use BACUP-converted Fallout 76 loading art and layout. Photos take priority when enabled.

settings.label: Menu Music Volume
settings.help: Zero mutes it.

settings.label: Mute Menu Music
settings.help: Mute without changing the volume.

settings.label: Photo Mode
settings.help: Adds PHOTO MODE to the pause menu.

settings.label: Freeze Time
settings.help: Pause the world while Photo Mode is open.

settings.label: Photo Folder
settings.help: Where confirmed photos are moved. Blank uses Fallout 4's screenshot folder; relative paths start there.

settings.label: Quick-Boy
settings.help: Allow the Quick-Boy overlay. Requires BACUP's Quick-Boy movie. Baka Fullscreen Pip-Boy keeps ownership when loaded.

settings.label: Pip-Boy View
settings.help: Use the normal Pip-Boy or the Quick-Boy overlay, including in power armor. Switching view in the Pip-Boy also saves this.

settings.label: Quick-Boy Size
settings.help: 1.0 is the source mesh size. Try 1.25 for a larger curved screen, up to 1.5. Check the edges for clipping.

settings.label: Quick-Boy Brightness
settings.help: Brighten menu text and icons without changing your color, the background or the arm view. 1.0 is the original brightness.

settings.label: L3 Switches View
settings.help: Reserve left stick click while the Pip-Boy has focus. Turn off if another mod uses L3.

settings.label: Quick-Boy Color
settings.help: Match Pip-Boy uses your Pip-Boy color on foot and the HUD color in power armor, as the arm Pip-Boy does.

settings.label: Own Color
settings.help: Used when Quick-Boy Color is Own Color; picking a color selects it.

settings.label: New Game Start
settings.help: Fallout 4 plays the prewar intro and Vault 111 as normal. Fallout 76 skips it and wakes you in Vault 76 on Reclamation Day; leaving the vault starts "Out of Time". Read once when a new game begins; existing saves keep their start.

settings.label: Playable Ghoul
settings.help: Requires BACUP's player_ghoul.json catalog.

settings.label: Weathered Appearance
settings.help: Apply the converted ghoul face and skin after leaving menus, combat and power armor.

settings.label: Original Appearance
settings.help: Restore the face and skin saved before ghoul customization. Ghoul gameplay remains active.

settings.label: Return to Human
settings.help: Return to human after closing menus, leaving combat and exiting power armor.

settings.label: Companion Progression
settings.help: Nearby travelling companions earn XP with you. Levels grant health, damage, automatic perks and stronger shared perk cards. View progress in Pip-Boy STAT > COMPANIONS. Off removes bonuses and keeps earned XP.

settings.label: Companion XP Rate (%)
settings.help: Percentage of your earned XP given to each nearby travelling companion, including modded teammates. 50 is half your XP; 100 is equal; 0 pauses XP. Requires Companion Progression.

settings.label: Multiple Companions
settings.help: Travel with one lead companion plus companions and allies in light slots. Recruiting someone makes them the lead and keeps the old lead on the team. Off sends extra light companions home.

settings.label: Light Companion Slots
settings.help: How many companions and allies travel beside the lead. Lowering it sends the extra ones home. Requires Multiple Companions.

settings.label: Companion Team HUD
settings.help: Show health and shared perk cards for recruited companions, including lite companions.

settings.label: Companion Face Portraits
settings.help: Render still portraits from companions' current appearance and equipment. Requires Companion Team HUD.

settings.label: Compact Team HUD
settings.help: Show only the portraits, each with a health and radiation meter: a bar beside square portraits, a ring around round ones. Names, health bars and shared perks are hidden. Until every companion has a portrait, the team keeps its full rows. Requires Companion Face Portraits.

settings.label: Companion Portrait Style
settings.help: Realistic shows the rendered model. Cartoon flattens it into cel shading with ink lines, closer to Fallout 76's Vault Boy art. HUD Tint keeps the portrait's detail in shades of the HUD color, like a Pip-Boy image; Silhouette is the companion's shape in the HUD color. Requires Companion Face Portraits.

settings.label: Companion Portrait Shape
settings.help: Square tiles, squares with rounded corners, or round portraits. Requires Companion Face Portraits.

settings.label: Companion Portrait Size
settings.help: How large the team portraits draw. The name and health bar move aside to make room, and larger portraits start a new column sooner. Requires Companion Face Portraits.

settings.label: Companion Portrait Framing
settings.help: Head and shoulders, or a headshot that zooms in on the face. Companions without a head show their whole body either way. Requires Companion Face Portraits.

settings.label: Companion Portrait Border
settings.help: Outline each portrait in the HUD color, red while the companion is downed. Requires Companion Face Portraits.

settings.label: Companion Portrait Shadow
settings.help: A drop shadow under each portrait: the companion's own shape, or the tile when a background is on. Requires Companion Face Portraits.

settings.label: Companion Portrait Background
settings.help: A tile behind each portrait, in grey or the HUD color, see-through or solid. It follows the portrait's shape. Requires Companion Face Portraits.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Quick Loot
settings.help: Use Fallout 76's quick-loot list and button prompts. Follows HUD Color and opacity.

settings.label: Area Loot
settings.help: Looting a corpse also lists the loot of every other corpse within the distance below.

settings.label: Area Loot in Quick Loot
settings.help: Include nearby corpses in the quick-loot menu. Turn off to use area loot only in the transfer window. Requires Area Loot.

settings.label: Corpse Highlight
settings.help: Dead actors that still hold loot glow like Fallout 76 corpses (orange for legendary actors).

settings.label: Unhighlight Corpses
settings.help: Stop highlighting after taking any loot, inspecting the corpse, or taking its last lootable item.

settings.label: Stack Area Loot
settings.help: Combine matching items from nearby corpses into one row. Taking that row draws from each corpse. Off keeps separate rows.

settings.label: Only Highlight Your Kills
settings.help: Only mark creatures whose death was credited to you or an active companion this session.

settings.label: Distance
settings.help: Game units, for both area loot and the highlight. Fallout 76 uses 2100.

settings.label: Highlight Refresh (seconds)
settings.help: How often nearby corpses are rescanned. Lower reacts faster, higher costs less.

settings.label: Equipment Condition
settings.help: Wear, enemy condition, broken-item blocking, repairs and condition bars.

settings.label: Item Levels
settings.help: All weapons and armor get an item level, as in Fallout 76: drops roll it, other gear takes yours. You can't equip one above your level, and its damage and resistances follow that level.

settings.label: Ranged Wear
settings.help: Condition lost per ranged shot. 1.0 is normal, 0 disables wear.

settings.label: Automatic Fire Wear
settings.help: Multiplies ranged wear for automatic weapons. 0.75 means 25% less wear per shot.

settings.label: Melee and Bash Wear
settings.help: Condition lost per melee hit or weapon bash. 1.0 is normal, 0 disables wear.

settings.label: Armor Wear
settings.help: Condition lost when armor or power armor takes damage. 1.0 is normal, 0 disables wear.

settings.label: Outfits Over Armor
settings.help: Equip outfits over underarmor and armor, for outfits from the base game and mods.

settings.label: Chassis Storage
settings.help: Collect a power armor frame as a Power Armor Chassis item; a frame you climb out of returns to your inventory after 60 seconds.

settings.label: Tracked Frames
settings.help: How many of your most recently used frames are watched for automatic recall.

settings.label: Legendary Weapons
settings.help: Legendary enemies can carry legendary weapons.

settings.label: Legendary Armor
settings.help: Legendary enemies can carry legendary armor.

settings.label: Prefer Equipped Weapon
settings.help: Make the enemy's equipped weapon the legendary drop when possible.

settings.label: Exclude Robots
settings.help: Robots never roll legendary.

settings.label: Exclude Turrets
settings.help: Turrets never roll legendary.

settings.label: Discover Effects From Plugins
settings.help: Also use legendary effects found in other plugins.

settings.label: Minimum Rank for Legendary Types
settings.help: Lowest star rank given to creatures the game already marks legendary.

settings.label: Base Chance Multiplier
settings.help: Scales the legendary chance for every enemy.

settings.label: Chance per Enemy Level
settings.help: Percent chance added per enemy level above the minimum.

settings.label: Maximum Chance
settings.help: Cap on an enemy's legendary chance, in percent.

settings.label: Minimum Enemy Level
settings.help: Enemies below this level never roll legendary.

settings.label: Maximum Effect Tier
settings.help: Maximum tier used when assigning discovered effects.

settings.label: Maximum Natural Stars
settings.help: Highest rank for new natural legendary enemies and their drops. Four stars is opt-in; five stays event-only.

settings.label: 1-Star Enemy Prefix
settings.help: Leave blank to keep the enemy's name.

settings.label: Item Name Prefix
settings.help: Text put before every legendary item's name.

settings.label: Effects in Item Names
settings.help: Name legendary items after their effects, as Fallout 76 does.

settings.label: Special Stock at Weapon Dealers Only
settings.help: Restrict random legendary weapons, legendary mod boxes and improved repair kits to weapon dealers. Off allows all caps vendors.

settings.label: Legendary Weapon Chance
settings.help: Percent chance per fresh vendor weapon to gain a legendary effect. Rolled once per restock.

settings.label: Improved Repair Kit Chance
settings.help: Percent chance of one improved repair kit per vendor restock.

settings.label: Legendary Mod Box Chance
settings.help: Percent chance of one usable 1-3-star legendary mod box per vendor restock.

settings.label: Scrap to Stash Chance
settings.help: Percent chance of one Scrap to Stash per vendor restock, at any vendor.

settings.label: Grahm's Stop Length (Game Hours)
settings.help: How long Grahm and Chally stay at each workshop, settlement or C.A.M.P. before walking to the next. Applies from the next stop after a load.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Hunger and Thirst
settings.help: Outside Survival, eating and drinking give Fallout 76's fed and hydrated buffs; empty needs cost nothing. Survival is unchanged.

settings.label: Always Show Hunger and Thirst
settings.help: Keep hunger and thirst bars visible while needs are active. Off keeps their current fade behavior. Requires Health Status.

settings.label: Food Spoilage
settings.help: Food spoils over play time as in Fallout 76, shown by its condition bar. Packaged food and drinks keep.

settings.label: Spoilage Speed
settings.help: Multiplies how fast all food spoils.

settings.label: Refrigerator Effect
settings.help: Scales Fallout 76's refrigerator rate (food inside spoils at half speed). Freezers stop spoilage.

settings.label: Spoiled Food Turns Rotten
settings.help: Fully spoiled food becomes Fallout 76's Spoiled Meat, Spoiled Vegetables and the like. Off leaves it at zero condition.

settings.label: Stored Food Spoils
settings.help: Food in your stash and in containers you store it in spoils too. Off, only carried food spoils.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Diseases
settings.help: Outside Survival you can catch Fallout 76's diseases from raw food, dirty water, toxic air, traps, dirty beds and Diseased creatures, from level 4 (level 15 near Vault 76). Disease Cure, Herbal Remedy and Antibiotics cure them.

settings.label: Disease Chance
settings.help: Multiplies every chance to catch a disease, after Endurance, resistance and perks.

settings.label: Diseased Creatures
settings.help: Some creatures appear as Diseased and can infect you when they hit you, as in Fallout 76.

settings.label: Disease Messages
settings.help: Shows when you catch a disease, what gave it to you, and when you recover, with Fallout 76's sounds.

settings.label: Symptom Reminders
settings.help: Repeats "You are suffering from..." every 45 or 90 seconds while you are sick. The symptoms still apply when off.

settings.label: Disease Risk Warnings
settings.help: Warns you in toxic air, dirty water and dirty beds, says when your gear protects you, and shows the disease icon on the HUD while you are at risk.

settings.label: Disease Timers
settings.help: Shows how long each disease has left on the Pip-Boy's Effects tab.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Respawn
settings.help: Move items from the enabled categories into your death container and choose a discovered map location. Off keeps Fallout 4's death flow. FO76 only applies while participating in a public event, Daily Op, or expedition mission.

settings.label: Drop Junk
settings.help: Drop junk and loose crafting components. Turn every drop category off to keep all items when respawning.

settings.label: Drop Aid
settings.help: Drop chems and other aid items. Food and drinks use their own toggle. Quest and favorited items stay with you.

settings.label: Drop Food and Drink
settings.help: Drop food and drinks, including water and Nuka-Cola.

settings.label: Drop Armor and Clothing
settings.help: Drop unequipped armor and clothing. Equipped, favorited and quest items stay with you.

settings.label: Drop Weapons
settings.help: Drop unequipped weapons with their attachments, names and condition. Equipped, favorited and quest items stay with you.

settings.label: Random Drop Amount
settings.help: Choose a random quantity from zero to the full count of each eligible stack. Off drops the whole stack. Applies only to enabled categories.

settings.label: Death Container
settings.help: Choose a converted Fallout 76 loot-bag appearance. Contents are preserved. An unavailable style falls back to the paper bag.

settings.label: Fallout 76 Infestations
settings.help: Rotating Infestations in Appalachia regions with a fog search area, a replacement faction and an elite four-star boss. Off stops new sites; active sites still finish.

settings.label: Simultaneous Infestations
settings.help: At most one per region.

settings.label: Game Hours Between Infestations
settings.help: How long to wait before trying to start another Infestation.

settings.label: Code Officer Fallback
settings.help: If the nuke-code officer quest will not start, or an officer never appears, Tales starts it and places the Scorched officers at random Appalachia locations. Off leaves it to the quest alone.

settings.label: Minutes Before Fallback
settings.help: How many one-minute checks the quest gets on its own first. 0 steps in at the first check.

settings.label: Launch Card Vertibot
settings.help: Keep Fallout 76's launch-card vertibot patrol in the air: an escorted vertibot drops the nuke launch card at a random location. The surveillance terminal tracks it. Off leaves only the terminal's own launch-card crate.

settings.label: Minutes Between Launch Card Patrols
settings.help: Wait after a patrol ends before the next one starts.

settings.label: Vertibot Patrols
settings.help: Hostile vertibots now and then circle a clearing near you, out of sight at first.

settings.label: Minutes Between Vertibot Patrols
settings.help: How often a patrol may appear; one at a time.

settings.label: Vertibot Patrol Chance (%)
settings.help: Chance that a patrol appears when one is due.

settings.label: Random Air Drops
settings.help: Now and then a government vertibot drops a supply crate at an air-drop marker some distance away, as when you use an air drop holotape at a radio station.

settings.label: Minutes Between Air Drops
settings.help: How often a random drop may come; never while another air drop is running.

settings.label: Air Drop Chance (%)
settings.help: Chance that a drop comes when one is due.

settings.label: Roaming Encounters
settings.help: Fallout 76's wandering bosses, creature hordes and swarms now and then appear near you in Appalachia. One at a time, never indoors, in combat or during a public event.

settings.label: Seconds Between Chances
settings.help: How often an encounter may appear. Fallout 76 used 600.

settings.label: Encounter Chance (%)
settings.help: Chance that an encounter appears when one is due.

settings.label: Minimum Level
settings.help: No roaming encounters before this character level.

settings.label: Hordes
settings.help: A legendary alpha with an entourage and a horde of its kind.

settings.label: Swarms
settings.help: Waves of one creature kind, sometimes ending with a legendary boss.

settings.label: Wandering Bosses
settings.help: A lone legendary creature patrolling the area.

settings.label: Spawn Distance
settings.help: How far from you an encounter starts, in game units.

settings.label: Abandon Distance
settings.help: Leave an encounter this far behind for five minutes and it ends, removing its creatures.

settings.label: Continuous Exploration Music
settings.help: Like Fallout 76, the exploration track keeps playing through outdoor cells that have no music of their own instead of restarting with a new track.

settings.label: Hold LOD at the Loaded Edge
settings.help: Distant LOD stays up until a newly loaded cell's objects have faded in, instead of popping out first.

settings.label: Edge Hold (s)
settings.help: How long distant LOD stays after the game would hide it.

settings.label: Crossfade LOD Levels
settings.help: Dither between distant LOD levels. Off keeps your Fallout4Prefs.ini crossfade settings.

settings.label: Level Fade (s)
settings.help: Length of a distant LOD level crossfade.

settings.label: Distance Preset
settings.help: Game keeps your Fallout4Prefs.ini LOD distances; Fallout 76 Ultra applies Fallout 76's.

settings.label: Large Precombine Mods
settings.help: Experimental. When another mod's precombine index would overflow the game's own and crash at startup (large worldspace mods loaded with SeventySix), keep that mod's index separately. Its precombines for Fallout 4's own cells are dropped.

settings.label: Raids
settings.help: Gleaming Depths can be started from the Fissure Site marker on the map.

settings.label: Recover at Checkpoint
settings.help: Dying inside a raid encounter returns you to its checkpoint and resets the encounter.

settings.label: XP Scale
settings.help: Fraction of Fallout 76's raid XP granted per encounter.

settings.label: Drill Fuel Needed
settings.help: Fallout 76 needs 15; 0 keeps its value.

settings.label: Drill Wave Size
settings.help: Solo default; 0 keeps the Fallout 76 value.

settings.label: Drill Suicider Cap
settings.help: Solo default; 0 keeps the Fallout 76 value.

settings.label: Drill Wave Interval (seconds)
settings.help: Solo default; 0 keeps the Fallout 76 value.

settings.label: Cap Stalker Damage
settings.help: The drill's stalker no longer kills in one hit.

settings.label: Stalker Damage Cap
settings.help: Largest fraction of your health one stalker hit can take.

settings.label: Squad Epsilon Eyebots
settings.help: Solo default; 0 keeps the Fallout 76 value.

settings.label: Eyebot Spawn Interval (seconds)
settings.help: Solo default; 0 keeps the Fallout 76 value.

settings.label: C.A.M.P. Build Menu
settings.help: Experimental converted Fallout 76 build interface. Uses the live workshop recipe tree.

settings.label: C.A.M.P. Build Camera
settings.help: Move the build camera inside your C.A.M.P. boundary. View toggles the camera on a controller; right stick click selects the overhead view. Left-stick click switches between camera and menu controls. Sticks move and look; D-pad up/down changes height.

settings.label: Stash Weight Limit
settings.help: Cap the weight your stash holds, as Fallout 76 does. Whatever would go over comes back to you. Scrapbox and ammo box contents don't count.

settings.label: Challenges
settings.help: Daily, weekly and lifetime challenges. While off, progress, rewards, HUD and the map panel are disabled; saved progress is kept.

settings.label: Perk Card Rewards
settings.help: Perk-card challenge rewards. Earned packs are kept while off.

settings.label: Realtime VATS
settings.help: Experimental FO76 VATS without slow motion. Tap VATS to lock on; hold for VANS. Guns and bows.

settings.label: Heal
settings.help: Use the available item with the highest health restoration. Fishing wins if both share a key.

settings.label: Start Fishing
settings.help: Start fishing when the fishing prompt appears.

settings.label: Switch Pip-Boy View
settings.help: Only while the Pip-Boy has focus.

settings.label: Open Photo Mode
settings.help: Opens Photo Mode in gameplay.

settings.label: Toggle Build Camera
settings.help: During C.A.M.P. building. WASD moves, mouse looks, Alt rises, Ctrl lowers and Shift moves faster.

settings.label: Overhead Build Camera
settings.help: Look down from inside the C.A.M.P. boundary.

settings.label: Build Camera / Menu Controls
settings.help: Keep the free camera in place while browsing the build menu. Left-stick click switches controls on a controller.

settings.label: Open Emote Wheel
settings.help: Opens the emote wheel in gameplay.

settings.label: Make Companion Lead
settings.help: Aim at a companion on your team and press to make them the lead. Requires Multiple Companions.

settings.label: Log Level
settings.help: Detail written to the Tales log in Documents/My Games/Fallout4/F4SE.

settings.label: Leveled List Trace
settings.help: Log every Fallout 76 leveled-list roll: list, subject, passing entries and the pick. Large logs; for diagnosis only.
